title: Verified weighted Hilbert–Schmidt least-change updates and the DFP specialization
description:
The displayed self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt secant perturbation uniquely minimizes the weighted Hilbert–Schmidt norm over all feasible perturbations on an arbitrary complete real inner-product space. Under the exact supplied invertible factor C and positive curvature, its weight is y and the DFP perturbation has the same feasibility, global minimality and uniqueness properties.

The new formal work transports the accepted PSB minimizer through the invertible congruence E(P)=R*PR, proves the required Hilbert–Schmidt summability, matches the displayed candidate, and transfers global minimality and uniqueness back to the original secant problem. The DFP specialization verifies the weight identity and applies that implementation.

Exact hypotheses: Complete real inner-product space H; any Hilbert basis b with arbitrary index type. No finite-dimensional or separability restriction. B : H →L[ℝ] H is self-adjoint. No positivity assumption is added. R : H ≃L[ℝ] H is a continuous linear equivalence; c = adjoint(R.symm)(R.symm s). y is arbitrary and s ≠ 0 for Proposition A.2. P is Hilbert–Schmidt relative to b, self-adjoint, and (B+P)s=y. hsNorm b (adjoint R ∘L P ∘L R); the proof establishes the required summability rather than relying on the nonsummable tsum default. 0 < ⟨y,s⟩ and a supplied continuous linear equivalence C with y=adjoint(C)(C s). R=C.symm; factor existence is outside this target.

Original mathematics: Jean Charles Gilbert and Claude Lemaréchal, Some Numerical Experiments with Variable Storage Quasi-Newton Algorithms, IIASA WP-88-121 (August 1988), pp. 28–30, Proposition A.2 and equations (A.6)–(A.8). Their attribution to Dennis and Moré (1977) is retained; that predecessor text was not independently audited. The exact IIASA PDF was inspected and hashed; papers are cited, not redistributed.

vebis supplied the accepted PSB proof and two Hilbert–Schmidt ideal-property lemma bodies. Exact original sources, target/submission IDs, hashes and transformations are preserved. The DFP file also embeds the newly accepted weighted implementation. Reused results are not counted as additional contributions. mikedeng1 supplied the platform formulation and its existing equation-reference repair; Shuze Chen’s prior statement confirmation is distinct from review of these proofs.
